observations: The synthetic kiosk pilot was observed across three weekday sessions and offered two navigation labels for the same service: 'start a request' and 'begin service'.
The visible event stream records 24 completed sessions and 7 abandoned sessions.
Eleven completed sessions and five abandoned sessions displayed both navigation labels before the recorded outcome.
The median pause between the first label display and the next recorded event was 18 seconds.
No event records a visitor's reason for pausing or abandoning, and one maintenance interval has no collected label-display events.

The labels were shown in different interface positions; the aggregate data do not identify individual sessions beyond the stated event categories, and the observer did not interview visitors or infer unrecorded intent.
interpretations: Within the recorded stream, the share of sessions displaying both labels differs between completed sessions and abandoned sessions, but this is a descriptive association rather than evidence that wording or label exposure caused an outcome.
The 18-second median describes recorded timing; it does not establish confusion, hesitation, comprehension, or intent.
Wording, position, device familiarity, missing maintenance-interval events, or another unmeasured factor could account for part or all of the observed difference.
uncertainties: The missing maintenance interval may change the observed exposure counts and outcome proportions.

The event stream does not reveal why visitors paused or abandoned, whether the two labels were encountered in a consistent order, or whether individual visitor and device characteristics differed across sessions.
Because wording and position changed together and there is no randomized or controlled comparison, their separate effects are unresolved.
The aggregate categories do not provide enough session-level linkage to test alternative explanations or establish a causal relationship.
additional_evidence_needed: Complete and quality-audited event capture for the maintenance interval, with session-level records that link label exposure, order, position, timing, and outcome while preserving privacy.
A randomized or counterbalanced comparison that varies wording and position separately, with pre-specified completion and abandonment measures.
Direct usability evidence such as interviews, surveys, or moderated testing about pauses, label interpretation, and abandonment reasons.
Independent checks of the event instrumentation and a comparison with an appropriate baseline or control cohort.

observations: The synthetic migration moved an audit log from audit-ledger-v1 to audit-ledger-v2 and provides a field map, dry-run report, rollback note, and post-deploy status snapshot.
actor_ref and event_kind are required in both versions; context_blob is optional in v1 and required in v2 only when event_kind is configuration.
The dry run processed 412 synthetic records and reported 3 records needing manual review.
The rollback note states that deployment can be reverted, but it does not record whether the three records were restored.
The status snapshot reports migration_complete=true and review_queue=3.
The field map has no entry describing event ordering during the deployment window, and the artifacts contain no person, credential, production-customer, or private operational data.
interpretations: The listed field requirements describe part of the schema transition, but they do not by themselves establish that every record was migrated correctly or that all behavioral invariants were preserved.

The dry-run result and review queue indicate records requiring attention; the completion flag reports a status, not independent proof that those records were resolved or that migration correctness was verified.
The rollback note documents a stated capability to revert, not evidence that rollback was exercised or that restoration was complete.
The missing deployment-window ordering rule leaves chronological integrity as an unresolved governance and auditability question.
uncertainties: It is unknown why each of the three records entered manual review, whether its v1-to-v2 values were reconciled, and whether any records remained unresolved.
It is unknown whether the rollback path was tested and whether it restored the reviewed records and related audit history.
The artifacts do not establish how events written during deployment are ordered, whether ordering is preserved across the transition, or which invariant would be used to verify it.
The post-deploy status snapshot is not independently tied to a record-level reconciliation or an immutable audit trail.
additional_evidence_needed: A record-level reconciliation for all 412 records, including the three manual-review cases, before-and-after values, exception disposition, and independent sign-off.
A controlled rollback exercise with logs showing what was restored, followed by a comparison against the pre-migration audit state.
An explicit deployment-window ordering specification plus representative event samples, sequence or timestamp checks, and evidence that the invariant holds across the transition.
An independently verifiable audit trail or replay/digest comparison that connects the status snapshot to the underlying records and preserves provenance for the reported queue.
